keyframe_review.note: 470,822 km2 (bbox 72.6-81.7 E, 14.5-21.8 N), including the west coast and Goa (gazetteer test). The Alauddin Bahman Shah page: 'By the time of his death the kingdom stretched from north to south from the Wainganga River to Krishna' and 'from Bhongir to Daulatabad', and was 'divided into four provinces'. That is a box of roughly 4.3 x 5.5 degrees (about 275k km2 before intersecting with the shape) and leaves out the Konkan coast, Goa (which the Vijayanagara page has Harihara I holding 'by 1374') and the Warangal country (taken 1424-25). The page gives no extent for 1359-1374, so the box is applied to the whole shape (confidence 2). Infobox area: none on the Bahmani page. [Repair 2026-10-24 (reviewer sa-04-c): this piece holds for 1352-1360 only (972 cells, about 246000 km2). Golconda (Hyderabad 40 km) is out until the 1361 cession (ledger; Musunuri Nayaks page, treaty of 1361), Mahur (Nanded 80 km) until its annexation by 1427 (Ahmad Shah I page; ledger) and the Raichur doab is in (captured 1347, lost to Vijayanagara by 1374). The box keeps the page's 1358 extent; the pages give the Bahmani sultanate no land beyond it before the events added below.]

ledger.note: 1347: Raichur fort. 'The Bahmani Sultanate captured the fort in 1347'; the page has the fort passing to the Vijayanagara kingdom after the Kakatiyas and being disputed 'for nearly two centuries' afterwards; the Raichur doab is the researcher's reading of the fort's country. Mirror of vijayanagara-empire /ledger (1347 loss, 1374 gain).

3 August 1347: Zafar Khan founds the Bahmani Sultanate. 'Ismail Mukh abdicated in Zafar Khan's favor, resulting in the establishment of the Bahmani Sultanate with its headquarters at Hasanabad' (Gulbarga); Bahmani page: crowned 3 August 1347, 'established an independent state on the Deccan'.

1350: first campaign against Warangal. Zafar Khan 'led his first campaign against Warangal in 1350' and Kapaya Nayaka 'ceded the Kaulas fortress'. Kaulas is not located by the page (approximate position, flagged for the gazetteer).

1361: Golconda ceded. Kapaya Nayaka 'had to cede various forts and territories, including Golconda' under Bahman Shah's pressure, and 'In 1361, he gifted to the Bahmani Sultan Mohammed Shah I the Turquoise throne of Warangal' as part of a treaty; the Golkonda page has the fort ceded 'during the reign of Bahmani Sultan Mohammed Shah I'. No page dates the cession itself, so 1361 (the treaty) is a bridge, as in musunuri-nayaks /ledger/3. Warangal itself stays with Kapaya (killed 1368) and then the Recherlas: the 'subjugated' of the Mohammed Shah I page is a suzerainty, not an annexation.

1368: war with Vijayanagara over the doab. 'The first recorded firearm use in South Asia came at the Battle of Adoni against Vijayanagara' (1368); 'Hasan fought many wars with Vijayanagara' (Alauddin Bahman Shah page, undated).

In retaliation the Bahmani army under Malik-ut-Tujjar 'first defeated him in Rohankhedaghat, then followed him to Burhanpur, ransacked the city and finally crushed his army in Laling'; Nasir Khan died days later on 18 September 1437. The page does not say what became of Berar, so the regain is a bridge (Berar is a Bahmani taraf in the Mahmud Gawan page's 1460s and asserts independence in 1490). 1437: Nasir Khan is crushed at Laling and dies on 18 September 1437; the war over Berar ends.

wars.outcome: 1350: Kapaya Nayaka cedes the Kaulas fortress; Mohammed Shah I 'successfully subjugated' Warangal and Vijayanagara (undated, gift of the Turquoise throne); Ahmad Shah I campaigned at Warangal 1424-1425.

wars.name: Bahmani-Vijayanagara wars
wars.outcome: Adoni 1368; Firuz Shah's victories 1398 and 1406; the 1407 tribute treaty; defeat in 1417; siege of the capital 1423; victory over Deva Raya II in 1443.
wars.note: The Mohammed Shah I page links a 'Bahmani-Vijayanagar War (1362-1367)', which was not opened.

wars.name: Mahur campaigns
wars.outcome: Three campaigns in 1426 led to the annexation of Mahur by 1427.

wars.name: Konkan War (Gujarat and Bahmani)

zones.text: Thana and Mahim on the Konkan coast

wars.outcome: Gujarat annexed Thana and Mahim from the Bahmani Sultanate (Gujarat page).

wars.name: Khandesh capture of Berar
wars.outcome: Nasir Khan captured Berar in 1435; the Bahmani army crushed him at Laling and he died on 18 September 1437 (Khandesh page).

wars.name: Gajapati attacks on the Bahmani Sultanate
wars.outcome: Mahur and Bidar forts taken 1457, Devarakonda 1458 and Telangana made a Gajapati feudatory, Berar attempt in 1461 abandoned.

wars.name: Mahmud Gawan's campaigns
wars.outcome: Kanjeeveram 1469, alliance c. 1470, Goa in February 1472 and the siege of Belgaum; an invasion from Malwa had been repelled in 1462.

wars.name: Breakup of the Bahmani Sultanate
wars.outcome: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Berar asserted independence in 1490; Qasim Barid I revolted at Bidar in 1492; Golconda ended Bahmani rule in 1518.

certainty.note: No treaty line is recorded on the pages opened (the 1407 treaty set a tribute). The Vijayanagara frontier on the Tungabhadra-Krishna doab, the Gajapati frontier in Telangana and the Malwa and Gujarat frontiers are approximate throughout.

notes:
Cliopatria row: one, 1352-1491. The page has the sultanate founded 3 August 1347 (new 1347 keyframe) and 'formally dissolved in 1527' (Bahmani page); Cliopatria's last Bahmani year is 1491 and the Bidar Sultanate (Barid Shahi) starts in 1492, so end = 1491. The nominal Bahmani sultans lived to 1527 as puppets of the Baridis; Golconda 'ended Bahmani rule' in 1518.
Shape problems: the 1352 shape (470k km2) is about twice the extent the Alauddin Bahman Shah page gives for 1358 (Wainganga to Krishna; Bhongir to Daulatabad) and holds Goa and the Konkan; it is also larger than the 1475 shape although Mahmud Gawan 'extended the sultanate to its greatest extent' (Bahmani page). Later extents 1359-1449 are unverified: page budget (5 pages, all used: Bahmani Sultanate, Mahmud Gawan, Alauddin Bahman Shah, Ahmad Shah I Wali, Mohammed Shah I; Vijayanagara and Kapilendra pages were opened for the Vijayanagara dossier).
Pages disagree: capital to Bidar 1429 (Bahmani page) or 1432 (Ahmad Shah I page); Ahmad Shah I died 1435 or 1436 on the same page. The Bahmani page's sultan table did not come through, so no ruler list is given.
Not recorded because no page opened carries them: the Gujarat-Bahmani Konkan war of 1429-1431 (Thane and Mahim; recorded in the Gujarat Sultanate dossier), Khandesh's capture of Berar in 1435 (Khandesh dossier), the Malwa wars (the Ahmad Shah I page lists 'Malwa (1425-1435), and against Gujarat (1425-1435)' without places; the Mahmud Gawan page has a Malwa invasion repelled in 1462), the 1472 Bahmani capture of Rajahmundry and Kondavidu from the Gajapatis (Gajapati dossier), Mahmud Gawan's reorganisation of the tarafs in 1473 (four to eight), his execution on 5 April 1481.
Counterparts that need dossiers: none beyond existing ones (musunuri-nayaks, recherla-nayaks, gajapati-kingdom, bijapur, ahmadnagar, berar, bidar, golconda). 'Raja of Mahur' is the page's own term. The Kaulas fort is not located by the page; the coordinates used are approximate and the name is flagged for the gazetteer; Mahur is not in the gazetteer (Nanded used).

Repair 2026-10-24 (reviewer sa-04-c; pages reopened: Musunuri Nayaks, Golkonda, Gujarat Sultanate, Khandesh Sultanate, Recherla Nayaks, Battle of Raichur, Mahmud Gawan, Ahmad Shah I Wali, Mohammed Shah I, Bahmani Sultanate). (1) The 1352-1374 box (the 1358 extent) is no longer followed by a silent jump to Cliopatria's 1375 shape: the western strip enters as a confidence-1 gain in 1375 (the Gujarat page has Thana and Mahim Bahmani in 1429), the eastern block (Warangal and Rachakonda) only in 1435 (Recherla page; the Musunuri page has the Recherlas dominant in Telangana from 1368 to 1435), Golconda in 1361 (treaty year, bridge; Musunuri page). The Mohammed Shah I page's 'successfully subjugated' Warangal is read as a suzerainty after the 1361 treaty, not an annexation, and no vassal event is recorded because musunuri-nayaks carries none. (2) The 1450 shape is adjusted: the Telangana block is kept to 1457 and dropped in 1458 (Kapilendra page), the 1458 loss narrowed to the cells the shapes drop. (3) 1469 Konkan gain added (Mahmud Gawan page: 'the entire Konkan'); the 1472 Goa gain widened to Belgaum and the Kanara coast. (4) Mirrors added: vijayanagara-empire (1347 gain and 1374 loss of the Raichur doab, from the Battle of Raichur and Vijayanagara pages), gujarat-sultanate (1429-1431 contest, 1431 loss of Thana and Mahim), khandesh-sultanate (Berar lost 1435, back 1437; the Khandesh page dates the Bahmani defeat of Nasir Khan to 1437, so khandesh-sultanate /ledger/4 (1437, confidence 1) agrees), recherla-nayaks (1435), musunuri-nayaks (1361). (5) Rejected: gajapati-kingdom /ledger/5, the 1472 Bahmani capture of Rajahmundry and Kondavidu. The Purushottama Deva page has it ('The Turko-Persian Bahamanis had equally captured ... Rajamahendravaram and Kondavidu', no year) but the Mahmud Gawan page, opened for this repair, names neither place and Cliopatria's Bahmani shapes have no cell at Rajahmundry in any year, so a gain here would sit outside every shape; gajapati-kingdom's own 1500 gain from bahmani-sultanate (Prataparudra at the Krishna) falls nine years after this dossier ends in 1491. The Mahmud Gawan page's 'from the Arabian Sea to the Bay of Bengal' is the only hint, with no place. (5b) So that the 1350 Kaulas and 1427 Mahur events show in the shapes, Kaulas (40 km) is added from 1350 and Mahur (Nanded 80 km) is carved out of the 1358 box until 1427; the Raichur doab is the 156-cell spec the bijapur-sultanate dossier uses. (6) Not done: a vassal_start/vassal_end pair for the Warangal suzerainty (no counterpart ledger); the ruler list (the Bahmani page's sultan table is empty; try List of Bahmani sultans); Cliopatria's Bahmani shapes never contain the Raichur doab, which this dossier adds for 1347-1374 only.
